Jane (ACME): Hey, billing team — we got an invoice spike yesterday (2.1M tokens) but the console/day dashboard shows ~350k. We're running the on-prem metering agent v2.3.1 in our VPC. Can someone help triage?

Emma (Support): Sorry to hear that, @Jane. Can you paste the agent id + host and any recent host events (reboots, maintenance)? Also attach the agent audit log if possible.

Jane (ACME): agent-id: acme-rt-09, host: ip-10-0-3-21.ec2.internal. We did a kernel patch & reboot at 2026-01-14T03:21:12Z (maintenance window). Audit log attached (snippet).

Jane (ACME): ```
2026-01-14T03:20:58Z INFO event queued seq=235017 ts=2026-01-14T03:20:58Z tokens=512
2026-01-14T03:21:12Z INFO host rebooting
2026-01-14T03:21:45Z INFO buffer flush start pending=124
2026-01-14T03:21:45Z INFO sending batch seq_start=234900 seq_end=235040
2026-01-14T03:21:45Z INFO ack received seq_end=235040 tokens=1,498,432
```

Emma (Support): Thanks — that flush at 03:21:45 looks suspicious (lots of tokens in one ack). Did you notice anything about NTP or clock jumps on the host?

Jane (ACME): We saw NTP drift warnings earlier that day from our monitoring. Not sure of magnitude.

Raj (SRE): tagging in. Pattern here: offline buffer flush after a reboot + clock skew can cause late-arriving events to be attributed to the wrong billing window. Two ways that manifests: (1) the agent records event timestamps when generated (wall-clock), but when it replays buffered events after reboot the collector sometimes attributes arrival-time timestamps too; (2) if replay produces overlapping seq windows due to wrap/bug, the billing pipeline may double-count until dedupe kicks in.

Lucas (Metering): A few more specifics from our side: agent v2.3.1 used a wall-clock-based event timestamp and a separate monotonic seq counter. During an unclean shutdown the buffered batch can be re-emitted with the original event timestamps, but the ingestion path earlier versions used arrival timestamps for aggregation buckets. If the host clock moved backwards or forwards during the window, those events can land in prior/next invoice intervals and appear as large spikes.

Emma (Support): Can you run these quick checks on the host and paste output?
- sudo systemctl status redwood-meter
- sudo journalctl -u redwood-meter -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80
- sudo chronyc sources || sudo ntpq -p
- ls -l /var/log/redwood/audit.log*

Jane (ACME): Pasting selective output:
```
$ sudo systemctl status redwood-meter
● redwood-meter.service - Redwood Metering Agent
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/redwood-meter.service; enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Thu 2026-01-14 03:21:47 UTC; 12h ago

$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-meter -n 60 --no-pager | tail -n 40
2026-01-14T03:20:58Z INFO event queued seq=235017 ts=2026-01-14T03:20:58Z tokens=512
2026-01-14T03:21:12Z WARN unclean-shutdown detected last_seq=235016
2026-01-14T03:21:45Z INFO buffer flush start pending=124
2026-01-14T03:21:45Z INFO sending batch seq_start=234900 seq_end=235040
2026-01-14T03:21:46Z INFO network send ok batch_id=bf-20260114-1545
2026-01-14T03:21:46Z INFO ack received seq_end=235040 tokens=1,498,432
2026-01-15T00:12:03Z WARN ntp offset=12.4s source=10.0.0.5
```

Lucas (Metering): That ntp offset line is the smoking gun — ~12s offset. With the observed behavior, the buffered events were generated before the reboot, but the collector ingestion used arrival time for aggregation and your billing window boundaries shifted. That explains why the invoice shows ~1.5M tokens attributed to that window while the live dashboard (which reconciles by event ts) shows ~350k.

Raj (SRE): One more thing — older agent versions had a shortcoming where dedupe relied solely on (agent_id, seqid) but under unclean shutdown seqid windows could overlap temporarily. We fixed this in v2.3.4 by adding a monotonic epoch that prevents seq reuse across restarts and by preferring event-generated timestamps for aggregation.

Emma (Support): Next steps (short):
1) Please upgrade agent to v2.3.4 (safe, non-disruptive). That includes both dedupe and monotonic epoch fixes.
2) Sync NTP on the host now: sudo chronyc -a makestep  (or sudo ntpdate -u pool.ntp.org).
3) Share the full /var/log/redwood/audit.log file for our reconcile job.
4) We'll run a server-side reconcile that dedups late-arriving batches and reassigns tokens to correct windows; if that reduces billed tokens we'll issue an adjustment.

Jane (ACME): OK doing upgrade now. ETA ~30m. I attached the full audit log to the ticket.

deploy-bot: release redwood-meter v2.3.4 promoted to stable (sha: b8f3a1c).

Emma (Support): Thanks — once you confirm upgrade & ntp sync, paste the agent health check: API /health output or `sudo redwood-meterctl status`. We'll then kick off reconcile.

Jane (ACME): Upgrade completed. health output: `{\"status\":\"ok\",\"agent_id\":\"acme-rt-09\",\"version\":\"2.3.4\"}`. chronyc now shows <=0.2s offset.

Lucas (Metering): Got the audit log. Running reconcile now — this may take ~30m. I see the large batch id bf-20260114-1545 in the audit; reconcile will check for duplicate seq ranges and reassign tokens based on event_ts where available.

Lucas (Metering): Reconcile result: found 1 overlapping batch window, identified 1,142,000 tokens attributed to wrong billing interval, marked 1 batch as duplicate. Flagging for billing adjustment.

Emma (Support): Good — we'll open a billing adjustment request. @Jane, you should see a credit on the next invoice; I'll add timeline details to the ticket. Anything else you need from us? :white_check_mark:

Jane (ACME): That's great, thank you. Can you also share recommended monitoring to catch this earlier?

Raj (SRE): Recommended quick monitors:
- alert if agent reports ntp offset > 2s
- alert on large buffer-flush events (pending > 100)
- track seq gap/overlap metric we added in 2.3.4 (meter.seq_overlap > 0)
- run nightly reconcile job for any hosts in 'offline-prone' networks

Emma (Support): Adding those to the playbook. Marking thread resolved for now — reopen if anything else shows up. :eyes:

Jane (ACME): Closing on my side. Thanks all!"
